title: 🏦 Vaya: an AI loan advisor that asks whether you can still afford to live
excerpt: Every loan comparison site asks the same question: which bank has the lowest rate? That question...
content_html:
Every loan comparison site asks the same question: which bank has the lowest rate?

That question has almost nothing to do with whether the loan will ruin you.

A 6.2% loan you can barely service is worse than a 6.8% one that leaves you room to breathe. A rate that resets after twelve promotional months is not a 6.2% loan at all. And none of the twenty banks whose products you are comparing has any interest in telling you that.

So we built Vaya around the question people are actually asking, which is: if I take this, can I still live?

🔗 Live demo: vaya-project.vercel.app — no signup, nothing to install.

👨‍💻 Source code:

Vaya — AI Loan Advisor for Vietnam

Vaya is a conversational AI loan advisor that compares loan products across major Vietnamese banks. Users describe their borrowing needs in natural language — "I have a house and want to borrow 12 million for studying" — and the system collects what's missing through natural dialogue, then returns ranked recommendations with full financial transparency: monthly payments, DTI ratios, risk assessments, eligibility recovery steps, and cashflow survival analysis.

The platform is built on one architectural contract: a deterministic Decision Engine owns every number, and the LLM only talks. The engine (pure functions, zero LLM involvement) filters, prices, scores, and ranks. The AI layer extracts intent, converses with the customer, narrates pre-computed results, and answers policy questions via RAG — it never calculates, scores, ranks, or decides eligibility.

Target users: Vietnamese consumers evaluating loan options across multiple banks.

Core value proposition: Unbiased, explainable loan…

What it does

Describe your situation in one sentence. No forms, no wizard. The homepage is a chat input, because that is the product. "Car loan ₫800M, income ₫30M/month" is enough to start.

It compares real products from 20+ Vietnamese banks. Rates, maximum amounts, terms, processing time, LTV caps — side by side, sortable, filterable, with the actual bank logos so you know who you are dealing with.

It simulates the repayment against your cashflow. Full amortisation, month by month. What you pay, what is interest, what is left. Charts you can hover, not a single number in a box.

It gives you a survival score. This is the part I would show you first. Vaya runs a Monte Carlo simulation over your income, expenses and existing debt, and tells you the probability that the loan pushes you underwater — plus DTI, PTI, LTV and disposable income, each with a plain-language explanation attached. If a loan is risky it does not just say "not suitable"; it suggests borrowing less, extending the term, increasing the down payment, or which expenses to cut to get back into safe territory.

It flips the market. There is a marketplace where you post an anonymous request and banks bid on it — the reverse of shopping across twenty websites. Every offer is displayed next to that bank's own public listed rate, because the gap between the two is the entire point. Banks see your amount, term and income band. They never see your name, phone or email.

It speaks three languages. English, Vietnamese, Chinese — everything, including the AI's explanations, not just the navigation.

And it has a proper dark mode, if you are the kind of person who checks. Toggle is in the navbar; right-click it to hand control back to your OS.

Under the hood

Tech stack
  • Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript
  • No Tailwind — a hand-written design system in a single stylesheet, ~5,500 lines, square corners and one brand green throughout
  • Custom SVG charts rather than a charting library, so the tooltips and the amortisation curves behave exactly as the product needs
  • Monte Carlo simulation in pure TypeScript for the survival score, running client-side
  • i18n via React context, ~600 keys per language, three sets kept strictly in sync
  • React Bits <MagicBento /> for the feature grid
  • Deployed on Vercel

A few things I enjoyed building more than expected: the reverse-auction board has no AI in it at all — it is a forum, and forums already work. The whole survival engine is pure functions, which meant the report generator could reuse it without a single API call. And retrofitting dark mode onto a 5,500-line stylesheet that three people were editing daily turned out to be the hardest CSS problem of the project, by a distance.

Where it came from

Vaya was built for the Alibaba Cloud FSI Hackathon by a team of four. Results are announced on 11 August, which means it is currently in that nice window where I can only improve the parts nobody is judging.

If you want the longer story of how it was built — the product decisions, the tooling, what we got wrong — the team wrote it up here:

  • 🐦 The full build thread on X
  • 💼 Write-up on LinkedIn

I would like your eyes on it

Genuinely, not rhetorically — the demo is open and takes about two minutes:

vaya-project.vercel.app

Three things I am unsure about and would love to be argued with on:

  1. Is the survival score legible to someone who is not a finance person? It is the most valuable thing in the product and the easiest thing to over-engineer into noise. Try it and tell me whether the number means anything to you.
  2. Does the reverse-auction marketplace feel like something you would actually use, or like a mechanic that only makes sense to the people who built it?
  3. Chat-first homepage — right call or annoying? We deliberately did not build a landing page with a "Get Started" button. Some people love it. Some people scroll looking for the marketing site.

Drop a comment with what broke, what confused you, or what you would cut. I will reply to all of them.

content_html_zh:
每个贷款比较网站都会问同样的问题：哪家银行的利率最低？

这个问题几乎与贷款是否会毁了你无关。

一笔你几乎无法偿还的 6.2% 的贷款比 6.8% 的让你有喘息空间的贷款更糟糕。 十二个促销月后重置的利率根本不是 6.2% 的贷款。 而您正在比较其产品的二十家银行中没有一家有兴趣告诉您这一点。

因此，我们围绕人们实际提出的问题构建了 Vaya，即：如果我接受这个，我还能活下去吗？

🔗 现场演示：vaya-project.vercel.app — 无需注册，无需安装。

👨‍💻源代码：

Vaya — 越南人工智能贷款顾问

Vaya 是一款对话式人工智能贷款顾问，可以比较越南主要银行的贷款产品。 用户用自然语言描述他们的借贷需求——“我有一套房子，想借1200万用于学习”——系统通过自然对话收集缺失的内容，然后以完全财务透明的方式返回排名建议：每月付款、DTI比率、风险评估、资格恢复步骤和现金流生存分析。

该平台建立在一个架构合同的基础上：确定性决策引擎拥有每一个数字，而法学硕士只进行对话。 引擎（纯函数，零法学硕士参与）过滤器、价格、分数和排名。 AI 层提取意图，与客户交谈，叙述预先计算的结果，并通过 RAG 回答政策问题 - 它从不计算、评分、排名或决定资格。

目标用户：评估多家银行贷款选择的越南消费者。

核心价值主张：公正、可解释的贷款……

它的作用

用一句话描述一下你的情况。 没有表格，没有向导。 主页是聊天输入，因为那是产品。 “车贷₫8亿，收入₫30M/月”就够起步了。

它比较了 20 多家越南银行的真实产品。 费率、最大金额、条款、处理时间、LTV 上限 — 并排、可排序、可过滤，带有实际的银行徽标，以便您知道您在与谁打交道。

它模拟您的现金流还款。 逐月全额摊销。 你付出什么，利息是多少，还剩下什么。 您可以悬停图表，而不是框中的单个数字。

它会给你一个生存分数。 这是我首先要向您展示的部分。 Vaya 对您的收入、支出和现有债务进行蒙特卡洛模拟，并告诉您贷款使您陷入困境的可能性 - 以及 DTI、PTI、LTV 和可支配收入，每项都附有简单语言的解释。 如果贷款有风险，它不仅仅会说“不适合”，还会说“不适合”。它建议减少借贷、延长期限、增加首付或削减哪些费用以回到安全区域。

它翻转了市场。 有一个市场，您可以在其中发布匿名请求，然后银行对其进行竞价 - 与在二十个网站上购物的过程相反。 每个报价都显示在该银行自己的公开列出的利率旁边，因为两者之间的差距就是整个点。 银行会查看您的金额、期限和收入范围。 他们永远不会看到您的姓名、电话或电子邮件。

它说三种语言。 英语、越南语、中文——一切，包括人工智能的解释，而不仅仅是导航。

如果你是那种喜欢检查的人，它有一个合适的黑暗模式。 切换位于导航栏中；右键单击它将控制权交还给您的操作系统。

2/ 生存评分页面——最具特色的界面

3/ 市场上的银行报价与列出的利率相抵触

4/ 银行筛选员

5/ 魔法便当

6/人工智能猫

在引擎盖下

Tech stack
  • Next.js 14 应用程序路由器、TypeScript
  • No Tailwind — 一个单一样式表中的手写设计系统，约 5,500 条线、方角和一个品牌绿色贯穿始终
  • 自定义 SVG 图表而不是图表库，因此工具提示和摊销曲线的行为完全符合产品需求
  • 在纯 TypeScript 中进行蒙特卡罗模拟以获得生存分数，运行客户端
  • i18n 通过 React 上下文，每种语言约 600 个键，三组严格保持同步
  • 用于功能网格的 React Bits <MagicBento />
  • 部署在 Vercel 上

有几件事我比预期更喜欢构建：反向拍卖委员会根本没有人工智能——它是一个论坛，而且论坛已经可以工作了。 整个生存引擎是纯函数，这意味着报告生成器可以重用它，而无需调用单个 API。 事实证明，将深色模式改造到三个人每天编辑的 5,500 行样式表上是该项目中最难的 CSS 问题。

它来自哪里

Vaya 是由四人团队为阿里云 FSI 黑客松打造的。 结果将于 8 月 11 日公布，这意味着目前正处于一个很好的窗口，我只能改进没有人评判的部分。

如果你想了解它是如何构建的更长的故事 - 产品决策、工具、我们犯的错误 - 团队将其写在这里：

  • 🐦 X 上的完整构建线程
  • 💼 在 LinkedIn 上发表评论

我希望你能注视它

真诚地，不是言辞——演示已经开放，大约需要两分钟：

vaya-project.vercel.app

我不确定并且愿意争论的三件事是：

  1. 生存分数对于非财务人员来说是否清晰？ 它是产品中最有价值的东西，也是最容易被过度设计而产生噪音的东西。 尝试一下并告诉我这个数字对你是否有意义。
  2. 反向拍卖市场是否感觉像您实际使用的东西，或者像一个只对构建它的人有意义的机制？
  3. 聊天优先的主页——正确的选择还是烦人的？ 我们故意没有构建带有“开始”按钮的登陆页面。 有些人喜欢它。 有些人滚动寻找营销网站。
